excerpt: You are living through the largest hunger crisis on earth, and nearly nine million of you have been driven from your homes.
paras: You are living through the largest hunger crisis on earth, and nearly nine million of you have been driven from your homes. Relief comes first, and peace above all. When it comes, your Nile farmland, your gold and your people will need capital that arrives as fast as the need. We will be ready to design it with you.

The world has answered only in part. The United Nations and its partners have asked for $2.9 billion for 2026, and less than half has come. The World Food Programme needs $402 million to feed families from October 2026 to March 2027. The World Bank works through UNICEF and the World Health Organization: $182 million in grants approved in January 2025 for health and safety nets, and $76.3 million in June 2025 for solar power and internet access.

The work ahead is plain, and it is worth saying plainly. Even before the war, seventy-four in every hundred of your city dwellers lived in slums. Each of you uses about 309 kilowatt hours of electricity a year, under a third of what a decent life needs. At the last count, in 2019, fewer than half of your young people completed lower secondary school. Shelter sets your Coverage today, at 26.3 out of 100, with power and schooling close behind. None of it can wait for long, and all of it waits for peace.

When peace comes, turn that same resolve toward every home in the country. Picture Perfect Sudan: a morning when every family cooks with clean fuel and sits down to a full table; when every tap runs clean and every home has a safe toilet; when every child walks to a school where a teacher is waiting, and reads with ease by the age of ten; when every mother lives within reach of a clinic with the lights on, and every young person finds work that pays. And no Sudanese falls below a decent life, because the nation has decided that none will.
quote: Peace first. Then capital as fast as the need, so that no Sudanese family goes hungry again.
